cards.title: Ai2 Launches OlmoEarth Platform for Continent-Scale Satellite Inference
cards.why_it_matters: If you work on geospatial ML or large-scale distributed inference, this is a detailed engineering walkthrough of a production system processing terabytes of satellite imagery at fractions of a penny per square kilometer.
cards.summary: Ai2's OlmoEarth Platform wraps their Earth observation foundation models (pretrained on ~10TB of multimodal satellite data) in end-to-end inference infrastructure. It splits jobs into CPU-bound data acquisition/preprocessing, GPU inference, and CPU postprocessing stages. The system covers continent-scale areas in roughly a day, handling multi-provider imagery alignment, projection normalization, and distributed failure recovery.

cards.title: LFM2.5-Encoders: 3.7× Faster Than ModernBERT-base at 8,192-Token CPU Inference
cards.why_it_matters: For production NLP pipelines running classifiers or intent routers on CPU with long contexts, this is a concrete, benchmarked alternative to ModernBERT with significantly better long-context latency.
cards.summary: LFM2.5-Encoder-230M and -350M are initialized from LFM2 causal decoder backbones, converted to bidirectional encoders via symmetric attention masks and non-causal convolutions, then trained with 30% MLM masking in two stages (1K then 8,192-token context). At 8,192 tokens on CPU, LFM2.5-Encoder-230M takes ~28s versus ~90s for ModernBERT-base (~3.7× faster). Encoder-350M ranks fourth across 14 models on 17 GLUE/SuperGLUE/multilingual tasks; the three ahead are all larger.

cards.title: Relay-OPD Fixes Prefix Failure in On-Policy Distillation, +5.73% Over Standard OPD
cards.why_it_matters: This directly addresses a known failure mode in on-policy distillation — prefix compounding errors — with a label-free fix that also cuts training trajectory length in half, relevant if you work on small-model reasoning or post-training.
cards.summary: Relay-OPD detects divergence between teacher and student continuations on failed prefixes as a handoff trigger, letting the teacher briefly take over to produce a corrected 'relay' trajectory before the student resumes. Using Qwen3-4B-Instruct-2507 as teacher and Qwen3-0.6B/1.7B non-thinking students on eight math benchmarks, it beats standard OPD by +5.73% and FastOPD by +1.49% (1.7B average), while reducing training trajectory length by over 50%.

cards.title: πR²: Reactive Real-Time Flow Policies Replan at ~25Hz Using Asynchronous Fast/Slow Channels
cards.why_it_matters: Closing the reactivity-latency gap in chunked action diffusion policies is a key open problem for robot manipulation; this shows a concrete working solution on real hardware with measurable success rate gains.
cards.summary: πR² addresses the open-loop latency problem in action-chunking flow policies by splitting conditioning into a fast proprioception channel (updated every tick) and a slow asynchronously updated vision-language channel. Built on diffusion forcing's per-position noise schedule, it treats in-flight actions as inpainting conditioning and emits actions in one denoising step per call. Finetuned from GR00T-N1.7 on a real xArm6+XHand, it replans at ~25Hz (every 40ms), improving success rates by up to 23% in simulation and 30% in real-world tasks over the strongest baseline.

cards.title: CARE: Nucleus-Style Confidence-Adaptive Expert Routing Beats Fixed Top-k MoE-LoRA
cards.why_it_matters: A drop-in, no-extra-parameters routing rule for MoE-LoRA that improves performance at matched compute is directly useful if you work with parameter-efficient fine-tuning or mixture-of-experts architectures.
cards.summary: CARE uses the router's output distribution as a per-token uncertainty signal: experts are activated in decreasing weight order until cumulative mass hits a threshold (nucleus-style), with a small extension when admitted experts disagree. A budget thermostat keeps average active experts at any target. Evaluated on LLaMA-3.1-8B and Qwen2.5-7B across commonsense, math, code, and knowledge tasks, CARE outperforms fixed top-k MoE-LoRA at matched compute and matches fixed k=4 while activating fewer experts. The same signals improve OOD detection over MSP and entropy baselines.

cards.title: Desktop-Delta Bench: New 2,013-Instance Diagnostic for GUI Transition Understanding in Computer-Use Agents
cards.why_it_matters: As agent evals mature, step-level causal verification benchmarks like this expose failure modes invisible to end-task-success metrics — important context for anyone building or evaluating desktop CUAs.
cards.summary: DDB introduces 2,013 human-verified instances from multi-app Linux trajectories (~15 apps, 50 task domains) targeting three failure dimensions: state verification, source tracking, and context-aware control. It includes 463 temporal-ordering instances (105 with cross-trajectory decoys) and 1,550 before-after action pairs. Across 8 model families, best non-decoy and decoy ordering exact-match rates are 65.1% and 65.7%. Click F1 reaches 0.96 versus 0.76 for drag; action family inference is harder than localization.

cards.title: VetClaw: Edge-Cloud Agentic System for Veterinary Disease Screening via VLM Zero-Shot Classification
cards.why_it_matters: A working multimodal agentic pipeline separating edge orchestration (OpenClaw) from server-side workflow (LangGraph) is a concrete architecture reference for production agent deployments, even outside the veterinary domain.
cards.summary: VetClaw pairs a camera edge device running OpenClaw (scheduling, tool access, notifications) with a server-hosted vision-language model orchestrated via LangGraph for stateful workflow management including input validation, safety checks, conditional routing, and failure handling. Results show image-only VLM prediction is limited, while symptom-guided and multimodal inputs improve zero-shot classification performance. The system demonstrates deterministic safety rules and escalation for uncertain cases.
